Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

disappoint verb

also disappointed, be disappointed, disappointing, disappointment, let down, I won’t let you down

classical

Cic. Fam. 1.6.2: nōn fallam opīniōnem tuam
Cic. Fam. 1.9.16: in quō ego spem fefellī … invidōrum

spem fallere

phrase: fallō, fallere, fefellī, falsum, with spem (or opīniōnem, expectation) and the genitive or possessive of the person

disappoint someone’s hopes

Latin says what is disappointed: the hope (spem) or the expectation (opīniōnem, exspectātiōnem). The hope can be the subject too: nē spēs eum fallat, so that he is not disappointed (Cic. Fam. 1.3, Lewis & Short). Alone, fallere is to deceive.

Other words

  • 1frūstror: long u (Lewis & Short leaves it unmarked). Made from frūstrā (Lewis & Short), whose u is long: de Vaan s.v. fraus derives it from *fraud-tro-, and Bennett cites an apex. Ruling: frūstrā with a long u.

    frūstror1, frūstrārī, frūstrātus sum — disappoint, let down; deceive

    verb, first conjugation, deponent, transitive · also used · classical · Ter. And. 374: saepe jam mē spēs haec frūstrāta est; Traupman 151: frūstror, disappoint

    From frūstrā, in vain: to make someone’s hope or effort come to nothing; also to deceive, to trick (Lewis & Short). In a passive sense, frūstrātus spē, disappointed in a hope (Vell. 2.21.2, Lewis & Short).

  • spē dējicī — be disappointed, lose one’s hope

    phrase: the passive of dējiciō with the ablative spē · also used · classical · Caes. BG 1.8.4 (Lewis & Short): eā spē dējectī

    Literally “thrown down from a hope”: the historians’ way of saying that a hope came to nothing.

Examples

  • Ā mē omnia summa in tē studia officiaque exspectā; nōn fallam opīniōnem tuam.

    Expect every devotion and service from me; I won’t disappoint you.Cic. Fam. 1.6.2

  • Ībō: etsī hercle saepe jam mē spēs haec frūstrāta est.

    I’ll go, though heaven knows this hope has often let me down before.Ter. And. 374

  • Vah, frūstrā sum igitur gāvīsus miser.

    Oh, so I was glad for nothing, poor me.Ter. Haut. 857

  • nōlī affectāre quod tibi nōn est datum, dēlūsa nē spēs ad querēlam reccidat

    don’t reach for what wasn’t given you, or your disappointed hope will fall back into complaintPhaedr. 3.18.14–15

See also hope, fail, look forward to.
